answer.rationale: The two symptoms with hard numbers are onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ), and onboarding friction plausibly upstream-causes part of the activation drop, so a single onboarding-simplification test addresses both with one slot. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifted SMB first-week activation) are the load-bearing claims for that choice, so those are the two I spend verification budget on: memory_31 is 64 days old and predates the current competitive environment, and memory_86 is the direct completion-rate claim, so if either fails to replicate in the archived record the plan should shift toward activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger metric drop directly. I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 shows the signup/revenue lift came with a 12-point early-retention fall and is flagged as non-durable, which is a direct conflict with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue rather than a one-quarter signup number. Downstream value risk is flagged because a pricing response would also reset price anchors for price-sensitive cohorts and contaminate future cohort comparisons, and because whichever result this experiment produces will itself be consolidated into durable memory that later sessions will treat as settled. I am running this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, with retention and qualified-pipeline guardrails alongside completion rate, so the lift is not accepted on activation metrics alone; the inherited memories describe direction, not magnitude, in the current competitive conditions, and I am treating the expected effect size as unresolved until this test reports.
